newsitem.title: POLAND: Universal group bids for newsstand chain.
newsitem.headline: Universal group bids for newsstand chain.

text.p: A consortium of Polish companies led by the trading company Universal SA on Monday offered to pay $80 million for a 40-percent stake in newsstand chain Ruch SA to rival a bid by a group involving France's Hachette.

"The offer concerns the purchase of 40 percent of (Ruch) shares for $80 million," the consortium, also grouping private television Polsat SA and soft drink producer and publisher Multico SA, said in a statement.
The consortium said it planned to invest a total of $200 million in Ruch, which dominates Poland's press distribution market with about 17,000 kiosks nation-wide.
The offer was made outside the official Ruch sale tender, in which a group of Polish investors led by Hachette Distribution Services has a right to be the sole bidder.
But deputy treasury minister Leszek Juchniewicz said last week the ministry might annul the deal if an offer by a domestic bidder proves better.

Juchniewicz, who has not yet seen the Universal group's offer, told Reuters the ministry would consider the bid provided that it was backed by banking guarantees. The group's statement said such guarantees were available.
"When the offer arrives, I will send it to relevant departments to compare it...and the decision should be taken within days," he said over telephone.

In December last year, the treasury ministry signed a initial agreement on selling Ruch to the Hachette consortium but Juchniewicz later criticised the French company for disclosing terms of the accord to the media.

The daily Nowa Europa has quoted Hachette's president Jean-Louis Nachury as saying his company would pay $84 million for a 75 percent stake in Ruch and then earmark a further $45 million for increasing its capital.
Juchniewicz then told a news conference that the ministry was seeking better terms for the deal with Hachette. @
The sale of Ruch, which netted 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys in 1995, to Hachette was strongly advocated by French President Jacques Chirac during his visit to Poland last year.
